desc:
Return the length of the longest contiguous subarray of nums whose product is strictly positive. If no subarray has a positive product, return 0.

The numbers can be huge, so do not compute the product itself: only the signs matter.

Examples: [1, -2, -3, 4] gives 4 (product 24); [-1, -2, -3, 0, 5] gives 2 (the subarray [-1, -2]).
hints: A product is positive exactly when it contains no zero and an even number of negatives. A zero splits the array into independent parts.
For subarrays ending at index i, keep the length of the longest one with a positive product and of the longest one with a negative product.
Positive x: pos = pos + 1, neg = neg + 1 if neg > 0 else 0. Negative x: swap roles, the new pos is neg + 1 if neg > 0 else 0, and the new neg is pos + 1. Zero resets both to 0.
editorial: Let pos and neg be the lengths of the longest subarrays ending at the current index whose product is positive / negative (0 when none exists). A positive x keeps signs: pos + 1 stays positive, and a negative run extends to neg + 1 only if one existed. A negative x flips signs: the new positive run is the old negative run plus one (if it existed), the new negative run is the old positive run plus one. A zero kills both runs.
The answer is the largest pos seen. This is the sign-only cousin of Maximum Product Subarray and avoids big numbers entirely. O(n) time, O(1) space.
